sections.skill: Understand equity, dilution and the main types of crowdfunding

questions.prompt: What do investors usually receive?
questions.intro: INVESTORS give money in exchange for EQUITY: a share of ownership, and often a say in decisions. If an investor pays 20,000 dollars for 20 percent of the company after the deal, the implied post-money value is 100,000 dollars and the founder now owns less of it (DILUTION). Investors expect a return, usually from growth. CROWDFUNDING raises money from many people online; reward crowdfunding gives backers a product or perk, and backers expect delivery. Equity crowdfunding sells ownership and has legal rules. Read terms carefully and get advice.

questions.prompt: A founder owns 100 percent and sells 30 percent of the company from her own shares. What does she keep?
questions.intro: If a founder owns 100 percent and sells 25 percent of the company from her own shares, with no new shares issued, she keeps 100 - 25 = 75 percent. If instead the company ISSUES NEW SHARES so an investor owns 25 percent after the deal, every earlier stake shrinks by the same factor: a founder who owned 80 percent keeps 80 x 0.75 = 60 percent (DILUTION). Post-money value implied by an investment = amount invested / percent bought. Example: 30,000 for 15 percent means 30,000 / 0.15 = 200,000.
